papers.title: Codeveloping a Clinical Pathway for Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection With Primary Care Providers: User-Centered Design Study.
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is the most common cause of health care-associated infectious diarrhea; however, variability in laboratory testing results in uncertainty in diagnosis and clinical decision-making. Recurrent CDI (rCDI), defined as the return of infection following initial treatment, continues to present significant clinical challenges due to limited therapeutic options. Although health care providers are familiar with vancomycin as first-line therapy for CDI, many are less familiar with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), despite its recommendation in clinical guide
papers.summary: This study used user-centered design to co-develop a clinical pathway for managing recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI) together with primary care providers. The work addresses diagnostic uncertainty from variable laboratory testing and limited provider familiarity with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), despite its guideline recommendation. The resulting pathway aims to standardize and improve rCDI care in primary care settings.

papers.title: Butyrate Triggers Neuronal Signaling via Release of Colonic Serotonin in a Microfluidic Model of Gut-Brain Axis.
papers.abstract: Host-microbiota interactions play a central role in regulating gastrointestinal and cardiometabolic physiology, yet the mechanistic pathways linking microbial metabolites to sensory neuronal activation remain poorly defined. In particular, the rapid signaling events through which short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate influence epithelial and neuronal function in the colon have not been fully resolved due to limitations of existing models. Here, we developed and validated a compartmentalized microfluidic tri-channel model that spatially organizes primary colonic epithelial cells, sensory neu
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
papers.summary: The authors developed a compartmentalized microfluidic tri-channel model that co-cultures primary colonic epithelial cells with sensory neurons to study gut-brain signaling. Using this system, they show that the microbial metabolite butyrate triggers neuronal signaling indirectly by stimulating colonic epithelial cells to release serotonin. This provides a mechanistic link between short-chain fatty acids and sensory neuronal activation in the colon.

papers.title: Rarefaction is better than robust Aitchison PCA and other compositional data analysis methods at controlling for uneven sequencing effort.
papers.abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. How best to account for this variation has been a persistent problem in the microbial ecology literature. Historically, rarefaction has been used in ecology and this practice was adopted by microbial ecologists. However, rarefaction has been strongly criticized, leading to the development of compositional data analysis and normalization methods. Therefore, I reassessed the benchmarking data that were generated by the developers of one such method, robust Aitchison PCA. I found num
papers.summary: This study reanalyzes benchmarking data originally used to promote robust Aitchison PCA and finds that simple rarefaction actually controls for uneven sequencing depth better than compositional data analysis methods. The author argues that rarefaction, despite past criticism, remains a superior approach for handling variation in amplicon sequencing effort.

papers.title: GLT-1 and alcohol.
papers.abstract: Glutamate transporter 1 (GLT-1) is responsible for the uptake of glutamate from the extracellular space, predominantly into astrocytes that insulate glutamatergic synapses. This transport is the primary method by which glutamate is removed from the synapse, as, unlike several other neurotransmitters, there is very little reuptake of glutamate by presynaptic neurons following release. As such, GLT-1 is crucial for homeostatic functioning of glutamatergic synapses, with disruptions such as excessive downregulation contributing to excitotoxicity. Alcohol is one example of an exogenous agent that
papers.summary: This review discusses the role of the glutamate transporter GLT-1, which clears glutamate from synapses primarily via astrocytes, in the neurobiology of alcohol. It highlights how alcohol-induced downregulation of GLT-1 can disrupt glutamatergic homeostasis and contribute to excitotoxicity, suggesting GLT-1 as a potential therapeutic target for alcohol-related disorders.

papers.title: Microbial-Derived Exerkines as a Model of Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: There has been a growing interest in the utilization of the gut microbiome as a therapeutic tool. The relationship between the gut microbiome and exercise provides a unique opportunity to maximize the therapeutic capacity of the gut microbiome. Here, we summarize the potential of leveraging the gut microbiome to confer the health benefits of exercise through a novel class of microbial metabolites termed microbial-derived exerkines (MDEs). We identify multiple candidate and established MDEs described in the literature (e.g., pipecolic acid, succinate, short-chain fatty acids, indole-3-propionic
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
papers.summary: This review proposes that gut microbiome-derived metabolites, termed microbial-derived exerkines (MDEs), could be harnessed as a drug discovery model to replicate the health benefits of exercise. The authors catalog candidate and established MDEs such as pipecolic acid, succinate, short-chain fatty acids, and indole-3-propionic acid, highlighting their therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Strollur: an R package for working with amplicon sequence data in R.
papers.abstract: Microbiologists are increasingly relying on R to analyze and visualize amplicon sequence data from microbiome studies. We present strollur, which is an open-source package that facilitates the import, export, and handling of amplicon sequence data within the R programming language.
papers.summary: Strollur is an open-source R package that simplifies importing, exporting, and manipulating amplicon sequence data for microbiome studies. It provides a lightweight alternative for R users who want to work with amplicon data without relying on heavier, more complex pipelines.

papers.title: Methods to Address Compositional Data Challenges in Clinical Studies for the Safety Assessment of Human Microbiome Perturbations.
papers.abstract: Advances in sequencing technologies have enabled increasingly detailed characterisation of the human microbiome in clinical studies, but interpretation of microbiome modulation which has relevance to health and disease characterisation or safety assessments remains methodologically challenging. Taxonomic profiles generated by amplicon or shotgun sequencing are inherently compositional, sparse, and limited by detection, which complicates differential abundance analysis and may lead to unstable or misleading conclusions, especially in low-biomass settings where contamination and under-detection
papers.summary: This paper reviews methodological challenges in analyzing human microbiome data from clinical safety studies, focusing on the compositional, sparse, and detection-limited nature of taxonomic profiles. It discusses how these properties complicate differential abundance analysis and can produce unstable or misleading conclusions, particularly in low-biomass samples prone to contamination. The authors propose approaches to address these issues for more reliable microbiome safety assessments.

papers.title: Activity and diversity of sulfate- and methane-based pathways of anaerobic chitin and N-acetylglucosamine degradation in marine sediments.
papers.abstract: Sulfate reduction is estimated to account for half of the organic carbon respiration in anoxic, organic-rich ocean sediments. Sulfate-reducing microorganisms (SRMs) typically oxidize simple carbon compounds, such as primary alcohols, or small fatty acids. However, much of the organic input to the seafloor is complex, driving interactions between terminal respirers, such as SRMs and methanogens, and primary degraders that initiate the breakdown of complex organic carbon. To explore how these interactions shape sediment microbiomes, we conducted multi-month microcosm experiments using serially d
papers.summary: This study used long-term microcosm experiments with marine sediments to investigate how sulfate-reducing microorganisms and methanogens interact with primary degraders during the breakdown of complex organic carbon substrates like chitin and N-acetylglucosamine. The findings reveal the activity and diversity of anaerobic microbial pathways involved in chitin degradation, highlighting the cooperative interactions that shape sediment microbiomes.

papers.title: Integrative holo-omic data analysis predicts interactions across the host-microbiome axis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the interplay between host organisms and their microbiomes is central to the development of sustainable food systems. However, high dimensionality and spurious associations remain major obstacles to extracting meaningful biological insight from multi-omic host-associated microbiome data; a challenge further exacerbated when "holo-omic" analyses across the host-microbiome boundary are considered. Here, we show that a computational method designed for multi-omic analysis in eukaryotes can be leveraged to integrate and analyze five layers of holo-omic data from porcine hosts and the
papers.summary: The authors demonstrate that a computational method originally developed for multi-omic analysis in eukaryotes can be repurposed to integrate five layers of holo-omic data spanning both porcine hosts and their microbiomes. This approach addresses key challenges in host-microbiome research, including high dimensionality and spurious associations, to predict biologically meaningful interactions across the host-microbiome axis. The work has implications for sustainable food systems by enabling more reliable multi-omic integration in agricultural species.

papers.title: Functional-Taxonomic Scaling Resolves Conflicting Average Genome Size Estimates Across Environmental Gradients.
papers.abstract: Community-level average genome size (AGS) is a key trait linking microbial diversity, functional potential, and eco-evolutionary strategy, yet estimates of AGS diverge markedly among common methods. Here, we introduce and validate a framework that adjudicates conflicting AGS estimates by testing which estimate yields a gap between scaled functional diversity and scaled taxonomic diversity that is consistent with the expected positive association between genome size and gene functional breadth. Across independent environmental gradients, metagenomic AGS estimates align with this framework and e
papers.summary: The authors introduce a framework to resolve disagreements among methods for estimating average genome size (AGS) in microbial communities by testing which estimate best matches the expected positive link between genome size and functional gene breadth. Across independent environmental gradients, metagenomic AGS estimates proved most consistent with this functional-taxonomic scaling framework.

papers.title: Microbial filtering and functional reprogramming in soil exposed to spent NCM battery black powder.
papers.abstract: Spent lithium-ion battery black powder is an emerging complex contaminant, which contains transition metals, residual electrolyte salts, and compounds derived from organic electrolytes or binders. Its ecological effects on soil microbiomes remain poorly understood. Here, we designed a soil microcosm experiment with using red soil exposed to a concentration gradient of black powder derived from nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) lithium-ion batteries. Samples were collected at two incubation time points and analyzed by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Black powder exposure produced a nonlinear taxono
papers.summary: This study used soil microcosms and shotgun metagenomics to examine how spent NCM lithium-ion battery black powder affects soil microbial communities. Exposure caused nonlinear shifts in taxonomic composition and functional gene profiles, suggesting that soil microbes are filtered by the contaminant and undergo functional reprogramming. The work highlights ecological risks of battery waste in soils.

papers.title: Design and evaluation of a streamlined enrichment method for faster co-detection of enteric bacterial pathogens in natural soils and environmental samples.
papers.abstract: This study developed a streamlined, sensitive and rapid method for co-detection of low concentrations of Salmonella enterica, Shigella flexneri, Listeria monocytogenes, and pathogenic Escherichia coli from soil. First, autoclaved soil from Iowa with serial dilutions of bacteria to confirm individual species recovery rates on selective agar by qPCR under varying primary enrichment times was used. All pathogens were detected by qPCR of colonies recovered from replicate sterile soils spiked with 10^1 or greater bacteria within 5 hours of enrichment. Shiga toxin expressing E. coli (STEC) and L. mo
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study presents a streamlined enrichment workflow that enables simultaneous detection of four enteric bacterial pathogens (Salmonella, Shigella, Listeria, and pathogenic E. coli) from soil samples within about 5 hours. Using selective agar combined with qPCR, the method reliably detected pathogens at concentrations as low as 10^1 CFU in spiked sterile soils, offering a faster alternative to conventional culture-based approaches.

papers.title: Microbes on the Mind: Multi-modal Neuroimaging Reveals Gut-Brain Axes in Infants.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome undergoes rapid maturation after birth and has been associated with cognition and mental health, yet its relation to early brain development remains poorly defined. We analyzed 223 typically developing children aged 0-3 years with multimodal MRI and paired fecal shotgun metagenomics. Microbiome-wide association analyses identified associations with cortical morphology, white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity. Ridge-regularized canonical correlation analysis identified two principal covariance patterns: a structural-metabolic mode and a functional-taxonomic m
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study paired fecal metagenomics with multimodal MRI in 223 typically developing children aged 0-3 years to test whether gut microbiome composition relates to early brain development. Microbiome-wide association analyses linked microbial features to cortical morphology, white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity, and canonical correlation analysis revealed two main covariance patterns: a structural-metabolic mode and a functional-taxonomic mode. The findings suggest that gut-brain axes are already detectable in infancy, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for protein database indexes that reduces the memory footprint of taxonomic classification by over a third compared to Kaiju, while maintaining comparable speed. The method extends run-block compression to scale better with alphabet size, enabling efficient metagenomic sequence classification against large reference databases like RefSeq.

papers.title: Improving Metagenomics Classification with Kmask: Entropy-Based Masking of Low-Complexity Regions.
papers.abstract: Accurate taxonomic classification in metagenomics is often compromised by low-complexity sequences, which lead to chance matches that in turn cause sequences to be misclassified. Here we present Kmask, an entropy-based masking tool implemented for use either standalone or as part of Kraken [1,2] database construction, which replaces low-entropy regions with Ns. Using a sliding window size aligned with Kraken's default k-mer length and parameters optimized across 12 control bacterial genomes spanning a broad range of GC content, Kmask efficiently removes low-complexity sequences while retaining
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kmask is an entropy-based masking tool that replaces low-complexity regions in metagenomic sequences with Ns to reduce spurious matches during taxonomic classification. It can be used standalone or integrated into Kraken database construction, with parameters optimized across 12 control bacterial genomes spanning a wide GC range. The tool aims to improve classification accuracy by removing low-complexity sequences that cause misclassification.

papers.title: "Quadrupling" the protein family space with global metagenomics.
papers.abstract: The known universe of protein families represents only a small fraction of nature's molecular diversity. From 40.3 billion predicted open reading frames across 40 446 metagenomes, 9540 metatranscriptomes, and 539 million proteins from 167 415 reference genomes, we identified 608 258 previously uncharacterized putative protein families with ≥100 members and 6.5 million families with ≥25 members, none matching known Pfam domains or reference proteins. This effort doubles the known repertoire of large families and quadruples that of smaller families. Integration of AlphaFold2-based structural pre
papers.summary: By mining over 40 billion predicted open reading frames from tens of thousands of metagenomes, metatranscriptomes, and reference genomes, the authors identified 608,258 previously uncharacterized protein families with at least 100 members, plus 6.5 million smaller families, none of which matched known Pfam domains or reference proteins. This roughly doubles the known repertoire of large protein families and quadruples that of smaller families, substantially expanding the known protein family space. AlphaFold2-based structural predictions were integrated to help characterize these novel families.

papers.title: Viral Metagenomic Sequencing Reveals Viral Codetection Patterns in Children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections, yet the frequency and composition of viral codetections in affected children have not been extensively profiled using unbiased sequencing approaches. Here, we performed viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs collected from 42 pediatric patients with confirmed RSV infection to characterize the codetection landscape. RSV was detected and genotyped in all specimens. Beyond RSV, we identified nine additional human respiratory viruses coexisting across the cohort; several of these fall outside th
papers.summary: This study used unbiased viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs from 42 children with confirmed RSV infection to profile which other viruses were present. RSV was detected and genotyped in every sample, and nine additional human respiratory viruses were found co-occurring across the cohort, including some not typically covered by standard diagnostic panels. The work highlights how metagenomic approaches can reveal a broader viral codetection landscape in pediatric respiratory infections than routine testing.

papers.title: Foundation models and taxonomy inference for metagenomics: A practical review.
papers.abstract: Taxonomic classification in metagenomics remains anchored in alignment-based methods and exact k-mer indexers, which provide calibrated, traceable species-level assignments at scale when reference coverage is comprehensive. This review synthesizes the progression of the field toward self-supervised, DNA-specific foundation models, clarifying where they add value and how they should be evaluated. We report a structured literature search with explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria, and then critically compare families of approaches along two axes of practical relevance: reference coverage (in
papers.summary: This review surveys the shift in metagenomic taxonomic classification from alignment-based and k-mer methods toward self-supervised DNA foundation models. It uses a structured literature search to compare approach families along practical axes such as reference coverage, clarifying where foundation models add value and how they should be evaluated.

papers.title: Microbial transmission and ecology of human and environmental microbial communities in childcare centers.
papers.abstract: Background Early-life microbial exposures profoundly impact lifelong health trajectories by shaping immune maturation and modulating disease risk, e.g. as described by the "hygiene hypothesis." Childcare facilities represent a critical yet understudied source of microbial exposures where preschool-aged children spend 7-10 hours daily during key developmental periods. This study presents the first multi-omic and multi-kingdom investigation of microbial transmission and community ecology across childcare environments, integrating microbiome samples from both high-touch and low-touch surfaces wit
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omic and multi-kingdom profiling to characterize microbial communities and transmission dynamics in childcare centers, sampling both high-touch and low-touch surfaces alongside human-associated microbiomes. It provides the first comprehensive view of how microbes are shared between children and their environment in these settings, with implications for early-life immune exposure and the hygiene hypothesis.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies for wastewater virome surveillance: targeted methods (amplicon- and probe-based) that sensitively detect known viruses, and untargeted approaches that can reveal novel pathogens. It also highlights bioinformatic pitfalls that can affect interpretation of wastewater sequencing data.

papers.title: Mallard super-shedders of avian influenza exhibit distinct cloacal microbial abundance profiles.
papers.abstract: In many infectious disease systems, a small fraction of hosts accounts for a disproportionate share of transmission, but the biological basis of this heterogeneity remains poorly resolved. In avian influenza, mallards show substantial variation in viral shedding, raising the possibility that only a subset of individuals contributes strongly to environmental contamination and onward spread. To examine whether host microbiome structure is associated with this variation, we experimentally infected wild, captive mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza virus. We characterized cloacal microbiom
papers.summary: This study experimentally infected captive wild mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza and profiled their cloacal microbiomes, finding that individuals with unusually high viral shedding ('super-shedders') had distinct microbial abundance profiles compared to low shedders. The results suggest host microbiome composition may help explain why a small fraction of birds drives most influenza transmission.

papers.title: Chestnut-quebracho tannins shape the fecal metabolome of weaned pigs through microbiota-dependent urolithin production.
papers.abstract: Chestnut and quebracho tannins may support gut health in weaned piglets, but their efficacy likely depends on farm environment and microbial capacity to convert tannins into bioactive metabolites. This study evaluated the effects of a blend of chestnut-derived hydrolysable tannins and quebracho-derived condensed tannins on growth performance, diarrhea occurrence, gut metagenome, and fecal metabolome in piglets reared under two commercial farm conditions. A total of 160 weaned piglets (initial body weight 6.53 ± 0.13 kg) were assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design comprising 2 weaning units (W1 a
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study tested whether a blend of chestnut (hydrolysable) and quebracho (condensed) tannins improves gut health in weaned piglets across two commercial farm environments. Tannin effects on growth, diarrhea, the gut metagenome, and fecal metabolome depended on the farm setting and on the microbiota's ability to convert tannins into bioactive urolithin metabolites. The findings suggest tannin supplements work through microbiota-dependent metabolism rather than directly.

papers.title: Network-guided synthesis of antagonistic microbiota for suppressing maize stalk rot disease.
papers.abstract: Plant-associated microbiomes play a crucial role in sustaining host health and fitness, but how pathogen invasion reshapes microbial interaction networks and how to leverage this for developing effective biocontrol strategies remain poorly understood. This study investigated the maize microbiome under Fusarium stalk rot stress by integrating large-scale amplicon sequencing, network refinement, and experimental validation. To distinguish biological interactions from spurious associations driven by environmental and geographic factors, we applied a refined analytical framework to filter out abio
papers.summary: This study used large-scale amplicon sequencing combined with network refinement to map how Fusarium stalk rot infection reshapes the maize microbiome interaction network. By filtering out environment- and geography-driven spurious associations, the authors identified antagonistic microbial taxa and synthesized a consortium that suppressed maize stalk rot disease in validation experiments. The work demonstrates a network-guided framework for designing effective biocontrol communities against plant pathogens.

papers.title: Leviathan: fast, memory-efficient, and scalable taxonomic and pathway profiling for (pan)genome-resolved metagenomics and metatranscriptomics.
papers.abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. Benchmarking alignment backends on synthetic
papers.summary: Leviathan is a new tool that combines fast alignment-free taxonomic profiling (Sylph) with pseudo-alignment-based gene quantification (Salmon) to enable integrated taxonomic and functional profiling of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes against custom genome- and pangenome-resolved reference databases. It outputs per-genome pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage, addressing the limited support for custom reference databases in existing functional profilers.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of rhizosphere soil microbiota in wild and cultivated Notopterygium incisum, an umbelliferae medicinal herb.
papers.abstract: Notopterygium incisum is not only a traditional Chinese medicine but also an endemic herb. Artificial domestication and large-scale cultivation are crucial for resolving the crisis of wild resources and the supply-demand imbalance of N. incisum, yet current techniques have failed to stably provide the herb medicine in good quality. Metagenomic analyses revealed significant differences in the rhizomicrobiota between wild and cultivated N. incisum, particularly in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly. The rhizomicrobiota of the wild N. incisum from 3 different sites with
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing to compare rhizosphere soil microbial communities between wild and cultivated Notopterygium incisum, a traditional Chinese medicinal herb. The authors found significant differences in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly processes between wild and cultivated plants, suggesting that domestication alters the rhizosphere microbiome. These findings may help explain quality differences in cultivated versus wild medicinal herbs.

papers.title: Salivary microbiome responses to chlorhexidine and Coriandrum sativum essential oil mouthwashes in patients with periodontitis in a randomized 2-week clinical trial.
papers.abstract: To compare the short-term salivary microbiome effects of a Coriandrum sativum essential oil (CSEO) mouthwash, chlorhexidine (CHX) as a benchmark comparator, and water in patients with periodontitis.
papers.summary: This randomized 2-week clinical trial compared how three mouthwashes—a Coriandrum sativum essential oil (CSEO) rinse, chlorhexidine (CHX), and water—affect the salivary microbiome in periodontitis patients. The study characterizes short-term shifts in oral bacterial communities, providing evidence on whether the plant-based CSEO rinse has a distinct or milder impact on the microbiome than the standard CHX antiseptic.

papers.title: A cross-families evaluation of using fecal samples as a method to study the amphibian gut microbiome.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays an important role in animals. Fecal samples are often used to study the gut microbiota because they are convenient to collect, allow for longitudinal sampling, and often necessary when studying rare and endangered species. In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of using fecal samples by characterizing and comparing the microbiota of feces and the gut (small intestine mucosa, large intestine mucosa) for representatives of seven amphibian families. This includes the first data from a salamander species. Additionally, we compared fecal samples before (pre-feces) and
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether fecal samples accurately represent the gut microbiome across seven amphibian families, including the first such data from a salamander. By comparing microbial communities in feces versus small and large intestine mucosa, the authors assess how well non-invasive fecal sampling captures the true gut microbiota in amphibians.

papers.title: Microbial community composition on polytetrafluoroethylene tape retrieved from implant screw channels: A cross-sectional high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing study.
papers.abstract: To identify the types of microorganisms colonizing the surface of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape used for sealing the central screw channel in implant prostheses and to evaluate their association with the duration of prosthetic functional loading.
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the microbial communities colonizing PTFE tape used to seal the central screw channels of implant prostheses. The authors examined whether the composition of these communities is associated with how long the prosthesis has been under functional loading. The findings provide insight into the microorganisms that colonize this clinically relevant implant surface over time.

papers.title: Deep-sea Microbial Dataset of the Antarctic Ocean (dsMDAO): A high-resolution deep-sea microbial dataset of the Antarctic Ocean reveals potential for taxonomic and functional diversity.
papers.abstract: Antarctic deep-sea ecosystems harboured unique and metabolically versatile micro-organisms that sustained key biogeochemical processes under extreme polar conditions. However, the genomic diversity and ecological functions of these sedimentary or deep-sea microbial communities remained largely unexplored. Here, we constructed a comprehensive deep-sea microbial dataset of the Antarctic Ocean (dsMDAO) by integrating three newly sequenced Prydz Bay sediment metagenomes with 22 publicly available datasets (9 seawater and 13 sediment samples), spanning water depths of ~300-3500 m. Genome binning yi
papers.summary: This paper presents dsMDAO, a high-resolution deep-sea microbial dataset for the Antarctic Ocean built by combining three newly sequenced Prydz Bay sediment metagenomes with 22 public datasets spanning ~300-3500 m depths. Genome binning recovered microbial genomes that reveal substantial taxonomic and functional diversity, highlighting the metabolic versatility of polar deep-sea communities. The resource provides a foundation for exploring biogeochemical roles of Antarctic deep-sea microorganisms.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterisation of Antibiotic Resistance in Anaerobic Digesters and Their Implications for Environmental Health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in environmental systems represents an emerging One Health challenge, with anaerobic digesters potentially serving as reservoirs of resistance-associated genetic features. This study analysed four publicly available anaerobic digester shotgun metagenomic datasets (M2, M3, M12 and M17) retrieved from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive to characterise microbial functions, resistance-associated annotations and antibiotic target loci. The datasets were generated using Illumina HiSeq 2000 sequencing and analysed through quality assessment, assembly, functional annotation
papers.summary: This study re-analyzed four public shotgun metagenomic datasets from anaerobic digesters to profile microbial functions, antibiotic resistance annotations, and antibiotic target loci. The authors highlight anaerobic digesters as potential environmental reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance, framing this as a One Health concern. The work is largely descriptive and based on existing datasets rather than new sampling or methods.

papers.title: Structural and Functional Characterisation of a Metagenome-Derived CYP108D18 Reveals an Unusual Dioxygen-Bound State and Selective Hydrocarbon Hydroxylation.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 enzymes form a large superfamily of monooxygenases capable of oxidising diverse substrates. Among them, members of the CYP108 family are recognised for their role in monoterpenoid oxidation. In this study, we report the identification and characterisation of a new CYP108 family member, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome derived from microbial communities in a geothermal hot spring located in northern Queensland, Australia. Taxonomic binning associated CYP108D18 with a Novosphingobium species, a genus well-known for its bioremediation potential. CYP108D18 was heterolo
papers.summary: Researchers identified and characterized a novel cytochrome P450 enzyme, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome of a geothermal hot spring microbial community, linking it to a Novosphingobium species. The enzyme displays an unusual dioxygen-bound state and selectively hydroxylates hydrocarbons, expanding knowledge of CYP108 family function beyond monoterpenoid oxidation.

papers.title: From Rhizosphere to Resistance: Microbe-Plant Interactions in Eco-Smart Biocontrol.
papers.abstract: The increasing limitations of chemical pesticides such as environmental pollution, pathogen resistance, and threats to human and ecosystem health have increased the demand for sustainable, biologically based crop protection methods. Eco-smart biocontrol has emerged as a game-changing paradigm that uses beneficial microorganisms associated with plants to suppress phytopathogens, boost plant immunity, and make agroecosystems more resilient over time. Moving beyond traditional single-strain biocontrol, eco-smart biocontrol integrates multi-omics discovery, artificial intelligence-assisted predict
papers.summary: This review examines how beneficial plant-associated microorganisms can be used as sustainable alternatives to chemical pesticides, suppressing pathogens and boosting plant immunity. It highlights how multi-omics and AI-assisted approaches are advancing the field beyond traditional single-strain biocontrol toward more resilient 'eco-smart' strategies.

papers.title: The Plant-Microbe Alliance for Environmental Restoration: From Nature-Inspired Solutions to Engineered Ecological Recovery.
papers.abstract: According to the United Nations, up to 40% of the world's terrestrial ecosystems are degraded and in need of ecological restoration. Here, we argue that ecosystem restoration requires not only the reintroduction of plant species but also the recovery of the biological interactions that sustain ecosystem functioning. Plants and their associated microbiomes form integrated functional units in which microorganisms contribute to nutrient cycling, stress tolerance, contaminant degradation and ecosystem resilience. These plant-microbe partnerships therefore represent a new opportunity for environmen
papers.summary: This review argues that effective ecological restoration requires not just replanting vegetation but also restoring the microbial communities that partner with plants. It highlights how plant-microbiome interactions drive nutrient cycling, stress tolerance, and contaminant degradation, positioning these partnerships as tools for engineered environmental recovery.

papers.title: Converting Equol Nonproducers to Producers: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
papers.abstract: Soy isoflavones have been associated with benefits for menopausal symptoms, cardiovascular health, and cognitive function, yet randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in Western countries have produced inconsistent results. A key factor may be equol, a metabolite of daidzein with stronger estrogenic and antioxidant effects, produced at lower rates in Western than in East Asian populations. This systematic review evaluates RCTs aimed at converting equol nonproducers to producers (CRD420251038428). We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for RCTs published between 1991 and 2025. Twelve RCTs (n
papers.summary: This systematic review examines 12 randomized clinical trials testing whether equol nonproducers can be converted to equol producers, a trait linked to stronger benefits from soy isoflavones for menopausal symptoms, cardiovascular health, and cognition. The review highlights that equol production varies by population and may explain inconsistent trial results in Western countries.

papers.title: LGTM: Gaussian process modulated neural topic modeling for longitudinal microbiome.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal microbiome data are key to understanding the dynamics of microbial communities and their relationships with the host and environment. However, analysis of such data is challenging due to high dimensionality, compositionality, irregular sampling and temporal dependencies on external covariates. Existing analytical approaches typically address only subsets of these challenges, limiting their ability to yield biologically interpretable insights. We introduce LGTM, a probabilistic modeling framework that combines flexible non-linear longitudinal modeling with interpretable topic-based
papers.summary: LGTM is a new probabilistic framework that combines Gaussian process-based longitudinal modeling with neural topic modeling to analyze longitudinal microbiome data. It addresses key challenges like high dimensionality, compositionality, irregular sampling, and temporal dependencies on external covariates, aiming to produce biologically interpretable topic-based insights into microbial community dynamics.

papers.title: Personalized whole-body modeling links gut microbiota to metabolic perturbations in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome has been linked to metabolic disturbances in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the mechanisms by which gut microbes might influence metabolic dysfunction in AD remain poorly understood. Previously, gut microbiome-personalized whole-body models of human metabolism have been applied to predict how altered gut microbiome compositions may influence metabolites in the blood of healthy aging individuals with increased risk of AD. However, these previous results have not been validated in AD. In this study, we aimed to test these prior predictions in a cohort of AD dementia
papers.summary: This study uses personalized whole-body metabolic models informed by gut microbiome composition to test whether microbial changes drive metabolic perturbations in Alzheimer's disease dementia. It validates prior predictions from healthy aging cohorts in an AD cohort, linking specific gut microbes to blood metabolite alterations. The work supports a mechanistic role for the gut microbiome in AD-associated metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: From predicted bacteriocins to ecological function.
papers.abstract: Genome and metagenome mining have uncovered large repertoires of predicted bacteriocin loci, but ecological interpretation has lagged behind discovery. This review uses bacteriocins as a focused model for a broader problem in antimicrobial gene prediction: sequence identifies encoded potential, but it does not establish expression, product deployment, target engagement, or community-level consequence. We distinguish four forms of bacteriocin "silence": transcriptional silence, where loci are not detectably expressed under tested conditions; conditional silence, where expression or activity eme
papers.summary: This review argues that while genomic and metagenomic mining has revealed many predicted bacteriocin loci, sequence data alone cannot establish whether these antimicrobial peptides are actually expressed, deployed, or functionally active in microbial communities. The authors distinguish four forms of bacteriocin 'silence'—transcriptional, conditional, and others—to frame a broader challenge in antimicrobial gene prediction: moving from encoded potential to demonstrated ecological function.

papers.title: Altered gut microbial functional landscape in children with pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection: an exploratory metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS), also known as MIS-C (Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children), is a severe post-infectious inflammatory condition associated with SARS-CoV-2 in children. While coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by SARS-CoV-2, primarily affects the respiratory system, growing evidence highlights gastrointestinal involvement and the relevance of the gut-lung axis in systemic inflammation. However, the taxonomic and, particularly, the functional landscape of the gut microbiome in children with PIMS remains insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory metagenomic study characterizes the gut microbiome in children with Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS/MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on functional rather than just taxonomic changes. The authors identify alterations in microbial functional pathways that may relate to the systemic inflammation seen in PIMS, highlighting the potential role of the gut-lung axis in this post-COVID condition.

papers.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome alterations across HPV infection.
papers.abstract: The cervicovaginal microbiome is a proposed modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, yet its relationship with viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) remains incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome changes in relation to HPV infection, considering viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state types (CSTs). It aims to clarify the proposed role of the microbiome as a modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, though the abstract does not report specific findings.

papers.title: Cross-platform, multi-cohort identification of a caries microbial signature.
papers.abstract: To identify a robust salivary microbial signature associated with caries using a cross-platform, multi-cohort design.
papers.summary: This study uses a cross-platform, multi-cohort design to identify a reproducible salivary microbial signature associated with dental caries. By validating the signature across different sequencing platforms and independent cohorts, the work aims to establish a robust microbial biomarker set for caries risk assessment.

papers.title: Gut microbiota characteristics of gastric cancer patients across distinct pathological stages and their associations with tumor and paratumor mucosal microbiota.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is closely associated with microbial dysbiosis; however, the spatial-temporal characteristics of the gut, paracancerous, and intratumoral microbiomes, as well as their interrelationships during tumor progression, remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to characterize these microbiomes in 85 GC patients from Northwest China using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and functional annotation. Clinical samples included feces, tumor tissues, and paratumor mucosal tissues (≥5 cm from the tumor margin), enabling comprehensive profiling of microbial composition at the phylum,
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to profile the gut, tumor, and paratumor mucosal microbiomes of 85 gastric cancer patients from Northwest China across different pathological stages. It characterizes microbial composition and functional potential at multiple body sites, aiming to link gut microbiota features with tumor and adjacent mucosal communities during cancer progression.

papers.title: Functional organization outweighs spatial separation in structuring microbial communities across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume.
papers.abstract: Petroleum-hydrocarbon plumes in groundwater are shaped by hydrological transport, redox conditions, and indigenous microbial activity. However, it remains unclear whether spatial differences among groundwater microbiomes primarily reflect physical separation among wells or ecological reorganization associated with distinct attenuation states within a plume.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether differences in groundwater microbial communities across a petroleum-hydrocarbon plume are driven mainly by physical distance between sampling wells or by ecological reorganization tied to different contaminant attenuation states. The authors find that functional organization—how microbial communities are structured by their metabolic roles and redox conditions—outweighs spatial separation in shaping community composition. This suggests that plume attenuation status, rather than well location alone, is the primary driver of microbiome variation.

papers.title: Microbial niches at the One Health interface: linking environmental factors, biomes, and disease dynamics.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities shape life at every stratum of environmental hierarchy, ranging from a wide spectrum of functionalities such as nutrient cycling processes that support ecosystem functioning in soil biome to those of intricate balance between disease causal and responsive immune defenses in animals. This review explores the roles of microbial niches in shaping pathogen persistence, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination, and host-microbe interactions at the human-animal-environment interface. Emphasis is placed on microbial community assembly, environmental drivers of pathogen survi
papers.summary: This review examines how microbial communities at the human-animal-environment interface influence pathogen persistence, antimicrobial resistance spread, and host-microbe interactions. It emphasizes community assembly processes and environmental drivers that shape pathogen survival across interconnected biomes. The work frames these dynamics within the One Health framework linking environmental factors to disease emergence.

papers.title: Metagenomic Tools as Predictive Approaches to Decipher Soil and Rhizosphere Microbial Communities and Their Functions for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for resilient and sustainable food production necessitates a comprehensive understanding of rhizosphere microbial communities and their functional roles in enhancing plant health, nutrient acquisition, stress resilience, and crop productivity, thereby supporting food security and sustainable agriculture. However, soil microbiomes are composed of complex and unculturable communities of beneficial microorganisms that drive critical ecosystem functions, which traditional culture methods cannot capture. This limits the understanding of their roles and impacts on plant health
papers.summary: This review examines how metagenomic tools can be used to characterize the complex, largely unculturable microbial communities in soil and the rhizosphere and to predict their functional roles in plant health and crop productivity. It argues that these culture-independent approaches are essential for advancing sustainable agriculture and food security.

papers.title: Digital intelligence-enabled tumor microbiome research: from mechanistic dissection to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated microbiomes are integral components of the tumor microenvironment, modulating tumorigenesis and progression through immune and metabolic pathways. Microbiome data are high-dimensional, sparse, and compositional, which limits conventional analytical approaches. Digital intelligence-an umbrella term encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), big-data analytics, and multi-omics integration-has emerged as a powerful paradigm for tumor microbiome research. In this review, we delineate the applications of digital intelligence across the full pipeline: intellig
papers.summary: This review describes how digital intelligence—AI, machine learning, big-data analytics, and multi-omics integration—is being applied to tumor microbiome research, from mechanistic studies to clinical translation. It highlights how these computational approaches address the high-dimensional, sparse, and compositional nature of microbiome data that limits conventional analysis.

papers.title: Genetic and microbiomics approaches allow the monitoring of the growth of Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus cultures and their environmental influences.
papers.abstract: Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus is cultured in industrial facilities to produce allergen extracts for allergy diagnosis and therapeutic treatment. In these facilities, mite growth and production should be monitored, and exhaustive quality control is mandatory to harvest mites, reach optimal expansion, and avoid potential microbial contamination. In this study, we explored genetic approaches to monitor the growth of five independent D. pteronyssinus cultures. Microbiological studies were performed to characterise the evolution of microbial communities during culture. Finally, we designed a qRT-P
papers.summary: This study used genetic and microbiomic methods to monitor the growth of Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (house dust mite) cultures in industrial allergen-production facilities. The authors tracked microbial community changes over time and developed a qRT-PCR assay to quantify mite growth, aiming to improve quality control and prevent contamination. The work provides practical tools for optimizing mite cultivation for allergy diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics-guided drug development in inflammatory bowel disease: from mucosal immune niches to precision therapy.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are now treated with an expanding set of biologics and small molecules, yet treatment selection remains largely empirical. Primary non-response, secondary loss of response, incomplete mucosal healing, fibrostenosis, and fistulizing disease show that conventional clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers do not capture how disease is organized within tissue. This review argues that the inflamed intestine is better viewed as a set of spatially structured mucosal immune niches rather than as uniform inflammation, with epithelial, myeloid, lymphoid, st
papers.summary: This review argues that inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) should be understood as a collection of spatially organized mucosal immune niches rather than uniform inflammation, and that spatial multi-omics can map these niches to guide more precise drug development and therapy selection. It highlights how current clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers fail to capture tissue-level disease organization, contributing to treatment non-response and complications like fibrosis and fistulas.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics, Machine Learning, and Single-Cell Analysis Provide Insights into Potential Multi-Target Candidate Mechanisms of Combined MAGL11 and Icaritin in Alleviating Imidazole Propionate-Driven Metabolic Intestinal Injury.
papers.abstract: Unhealthy diets, especially high red meat intake, induce gut dysbiosis and abnormal accumulation of a harmful histidine metabolite imidazole propionate (IMP), thereby promoting ulcerative colitis (UC) development. Although combined treatment with a MAGL inhibitor (MAGL11) and icaritin (Y003) exerts combined therapeutic effects in the classical DSS‑induced UC model, its protective effects and molecular mechanisms against IMP‑driven metabolic model remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether combining a MAGL inhibitor (MAGL11) with icaritin (Y003) can protect against intestinal injury caused by imidazole propionate (IMP), a harmful metabolite produced by gut bacteria after high red meat consumption. Using integrated multi-omics, machine learning, and single-cell analysis, the authors identify potential multi-target mechanisms underlying the combined treatment's protective effects in a metabolic model of ulcerative colitis.

papers.title: Correlation analysis between tongue hyperspectral imaging and tongue coating microbiota and feasibility study for early screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus status.
papers.abstract: To investigate the feasibility of applying hyperspectral imaging technology combined with machine learning algorithms for early non-invasive screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
papers.summary: This study explores whether hyperspectral imaging of the tongue, combined with machine learning, can non-invasively screen for type 2 diabetes. The authors correlate tongue imaging features with tongue coating microbiota, suggesting a link between spectral signatures and microbial composition. The work is a feasibility study, so results are preliminary and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism: a critical bridge linking gut microbiota to depression.
papers.abstract: Depression is a major global public health challenge with limitations in current therapies. Emerging evidence highlights that gut microbiota (GM) critically regulates the gut-brain axis via tryptophan (Trp) metabolism. Trp is metabolized through host-directed serotonin (5-HT) and kynurenine (KYN) pathways, as well as microbiota-specific indole derivative pathways. In depression, gut dysbiosis shifts Trp metabolism toward the KYN pathway, leading to accumulation of neurotoxic metabolites such as quinolinic acid and reduced 5-HT synthesis. Microbiota-derived indoles, functioning as key aryl hydr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that gut microbiota regulate the gut-brain axis through tryptophan metabolism, with dysbiosis in depression shifting tryptophan toward the neurotoxic kynurenine pathway and reducing serotonin synthesis. Microbiota-derived indole derivatives are highlighted as key modulators of this process, suggesting tryptophan metabolism as a therapeutic target for depression.

papers.title: Gut microbiota signatures in mild cognitive impairment: a scoping review of microbial taxa and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: To identify systematically the typical gut microbiota in mild cognitive impairment patients and its association in disease progression. Systematically identify microbial taxa consistently associated with Mild Cognitive Impairment.
papers.summary: This scoping review systematically compiles studies on gut microbiota composition in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), aiming to identify microbial taxa consistently associated with the condition. It highlights recurring signatures and discusses their potential link to disease progression and clinical implications, though heterogeneity across studies limits firm conclusions.

papers.title: NeighborFinder: an R package inferring local microbial network around a species of interest.
papers.abstract: Understanding interactions from microbiome data is a central aspect in microbial ecology, as it provides insights into ecosystem stability, disease mechanisms, and can be used to design synthetic communities. Current network inference tools reconstruct global networks from co-abundance data, which means they capture the overall correlation structure for the entire set of taxa considered. These approaches are computationally intensive and suboptimal when the focus is on the local neighborhood of one or a few taxa of interest.
papers.summary: NeighborFinder is an R package that infers the local microbial interaction network surrounding a species of interest, rather than reconstructing a full global co-abundance network. This targeted approach is more computationally efficient and better suited for studies focused on one or a few taxa, with applications in microbial ecology, disease research, and synthetic community design.

papers.title: Crotoxin from Crotalus durissus terrificus impairs the establishment of chemically induced colitis in mice associated with formyl peptide receptor signaling.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs) arise from a breakdown in tolerance to intestinal microbiota and are characterized by exacerbated inflammatory responses. Epithelial cells of the gastrointestinal tract play a central role in maintaining barrier integrity and orchestrating immune responses; however, the mechanisms underlying epithelial dysfunction and uncontrolled inflammation remain incompletely understood. Crotoxin (CTX), the main component of Crotalus d. terrificus venom, exhibits immunomodulatory activity, making it a promising tool to investigate epithelial-immune interactions in intesti
papers.summary: This study shows that crotoxin, a component of rattlesnake venom, can prevent the development of chemically induced colitis in mice. The protective effect appears to work through formyl peptide receptor signaling, suggesting a new mechanism for modulating intestinal inflammation. The findings highlight crotoxin as a potential tool for studying epithelial-immune interactions in inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning uncovers core seminal microbial signatures in idiopathic oligoasthenospermia.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have confirmed that changes in semen microbiota are closely related to male oligoasthenospermia(OA). However, current research only qualitatively describes the differences in the microbial community, fails to screen out core markers with independent discriminatory value, and also fails to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of the microbial community, resulting in insufficient research on the diagnostic value of the semen microbiota in oligoasthenospermia.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study applies interpretable machine learning to semen microbiome data to identify core microbial signatures that can distinguish idiopathic oligoasthenospermia from controls. The authors move beyond qualitative community descriptions to quantitatively evaluate diagnostic efficacy and screen for markers with independent discriminatory value.

papers.title: Beyond a universal obesity microbiome signature: pre-intervention heterogeneity and a framework for baseline profiling.
papers.abstract: Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize obesity-associated microbial alterations, this review reframes the recurrent inconsistency of human obesity microbiome findings as an informative consequence of pre-intervention heterogeneity rather than merely failed replication or analytical noise. We integrate biological and contextual determinants of baseline microbiota variation with methodological and analytical sources of heterogeneity into a unified framework for interpreting why microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and functional signals differ across individuals, populations, an
papers.summary: This review argues that inconsistent findings in human obesity microbiome studies are not simply replication failures but reflect meaningful pre-intervention heterogeneity in baseline microbiota across individuals and populations. It integrates biological, contextual, methodological, and analytical sources of variation into a unified framework for baseline profiling, aiming to guide more interpretable and personalized microbiome research in obesity.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Etiology-Specific Evidence, Mechanisms, and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) usually develops in patients with chronic liver disease and remains a major cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Increasing evidence suggests that dysbiosis of the gut microbiota is related to hepatocarcinogenesis through the gut-liver axis. Patients with HCC often show enrichment of pro-inflammatory or endotoxin-producing bacteria and loss of short-chain fatty acid-producing and barrier-protective taxa. These changes may increase intestinal permeability and microbial translocation and may contribute to chronic hepatic inflammation, immune disturbance, and me
papers.summary: This review examines how disruptions in gut microbiota composition are linked to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through the gut-liver axis, with HCC patients showing increased pro-inflammatory and endotoxin-producing bacteria alongside reduced beneficial short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa. These microbial shifts may promote liver cancer by increasing intestinal permeability, driving chronic hepatic inflammation, and disturbing immune function, though the authors highlight remaining translational challenges.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration of the vaginal microbiome and inflammatory proteome for non-invasive prediction of infertility: a machine learning approach.
papers.abstract: Infertility remains a global health challenge that often necessitates invasive and costly diagnostic procedures. While the vaginal microenvironment is known to influence reproductive health, its potential as a source of non-invasive biomarkers for infertility remains insufficiently explored. This study integrated vaginal microbiome and inflammatory proteomic profiling using machine learning to develop and validate an objective, non-invasive diagnostic model for identifying women at high risk of infertility.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study combined vaginal microbiome profiling with inflammatory protein measurements and applied machine learning to build a non-invasive model for predicting infertility risk in women. The integrated multi-omics approach reportedly distinguished high-risk individuals without requiring invasive diagnostic procedures. The work suggests vaginal microbial and inflammatory signatures could serve as accessible biomarkers for reproductive health screening.
